I will start from what I did last year and only push a little harder where I think the money can come back. I have 16.1 mu, so I cannot farm too cautiously like a tiny household plot, but I also cannot throw money around. Since I have only farmed 3 years, I will mostly follow what I have seen work around Quzhou. For wheat and maize, I will keep them steady because those are the safer crops and the rates around here are already well known. For cabbage, cauliflower, and eggplant, I will feed them heavier because vegetables take more out of the land and I would rather spend some extra fertilizer than lose yield. I have well irrigation, so I will use water to keep fertilizer working instead of letting it sit dry in the soil. I will use improved or hybrid seed where that has already shown good stand and yield locally, especially for eggplant and the brassica crops. On tillage, I will plough for wheat and the vegetable land so the base fertilizer can go down well, and I will use rotary tillage for maize to save time and cost. I will keep pesticide sprays to the level I think I can afford without letting insects and disease get ahead of me, because once vegetables get damaged, the loss is fast and real.
